:::{#sol-epe-split-noise}

Write the prediction error as noise plus the error of the prediction, used as an [estimator](estimation.qmd#def-estimator) of the [mean function](#def-mean-function) value $\mean(\predvar)$:

$$
\ba
\newoutvar - \predvalf{\predvar}
&= \paren{\newoutvar - \mean(\predvar)} + \paren{\mean(\predvar) - \predvalf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(add and subtract } \mean(\predvar) \text{)} \\
&= \noise + \paren{\mean(\predvar) - \predvalf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(definition of } \newoutvar \text{)}
\ea
$$

Square it:

$$
\ba
\sqf{\newoutvar - \predvalf{\predvar}}
&= \noise^2
+ 2 \noise \paren{\mean(\predvar) - \predvalf{\predvar}}
+ \sqf{\mean(\predvar) - \predvalf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(expand the square of a sum)}
\ea
$$

Take the expectation of each term in turn, using
[linearity of expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-linearity-expectation)
to split the sum.

For the noise term,
the [variance identity](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-variance)
gives $\varpar = \E{\noise^2} - \sqf{\E{\noise}}$:

$$
\ba
\E{\noise^2}
&= \varpar + \sqf{\E{\noise}}
&& \text{(variance identity)} \\
&= \varpar + 0^2
&& \text{(the noise has mean } 0 \text{)} \\
&= \varpar
&& \text{(} 0^2 = 0 \text{, and } \varpar + 0 = \varpar \text{)}
\ea
$$

For the cross term,
$\noise = \newoutvar - \mean(\predvar)$ shifts $\newoutvar$ by a constant,
and $\newoutvar$ is independent of $\trainset$,
so $\noise$ is independent of $\trainset$,
and hence of $\predvalf{\predvar}$ and of $\mean(\predvar) - \predvalf{\predvar}$.
The expectation of a product of independent random variables is the product of their expectations:

$$
\ba
\E{2 \noise \paren{\mean(\predvar) - \predvalf{\predvar}}}
&= 2 \E{\noise \paren{\mean(\predvar) - \predvalf{\predvar}}}
&& \text{(constant factor 2)} \\
&= 2 \E{\noise} \E{\mean(\predvar) - \predvalf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(independence)} \\
&= 2 \cdot 0 \cdot \E{\mean(\predvar) - \predvalf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(the noise has mean } 0 \text{)} \\
&= 0
&& \text{(zero times a number)}
\ea
$$

Adding the three expectations,

$$
\E{\sqf{\newoutvar - \predvalf{\predvar}}}
= \varpar + \E{\sqf{\mean(\predvar) - \predvalf{\predvar}}}.
$$ {#eq-epe-after-noise}

The cross term vanished because the noise has mean $0$ and,
for a new outcome, is independent of the training set.
Without the zero mean, independence alone would leave $2 \E{\noise}$ times $\E{\mean(\predvar) - \predvalf{\predvar}}$, which need not be zero.
That holds for a fresh observation,
and it fails for an observation the procedure was trained on,
whose noise helped determine the prediction.

:::
